note: Five cases. Run each in a fresh context, with and without the skill, and record the delta. Assertions are checked against the artifacts on disk, not against the transcript.

baseline.method: The worked-example deck was first built without this skill, as a 1,349-line build_deck.py that mixed content with ~350 lines of layout helpers.
baseline.failure: The unaided build produced a deck that was structurally valid and visually wrong in five ways, each found only by rendering: theme drop shadows on every shape, every panel's text silently centred, a two-line title overlapping its subtitle, a literal newline inside a run, and a caption drawn on top of a panel. Three further defects survived into the port and were found by `check`, not by eye. Separately, the deck that came out of the process was academically weak in ways only rendering and review cannot see: a research question whose subject was the case rather than the class, and a contribution that was bounded in every sentence and never claimed. A real first assessment of that thesis put ten of fifteen lost points into four of those academic failures while praising the methodology.

results.worked_deck: The 32-slide DSR colloquium deck (21 talk, 11 backup), the artifact this skill was extracted from, re-run through every verb after the academic upgrade.

deterministic.check: 0 errors, 0 warnings — including the new `figure` check, after alt text was added to all six pictures
deterministic.render: 32 PNGs + 4 contact sheets; contact sheets inspected, unchanged
deterministic.readiness: ran; argument skeleton read; five questions answered with findings keyed to slides 1, 7, 11, 14, 18, 19
deterministic.timing: 1,548 spoken words — 12:23 at 125 wpm against a noted 10:00 budget; 10 slides with a script longer than their slot
deterministic.handout: 32 pages, 4.1 MB, German quotes and en dashes render correctly

results.delta: The academic layer surfaced five findings the unaided process produced no mechanism to see: (1) the spoken script is 2:23 over the ten-minute budget at a deliberate pace; (2) the positioning slide reproduced the engineering-columns matrix the written assessment criticised, with no construct column; (3) the title claims a class the evidence does not cover and no talk slide concedes it; (4) the contribution is claimed well but its type is named only on a backup slide; (5) the DSRM figure was a local rebuild rather than the published original, with no visible source line. Findings 2-4 remain open content decisions; 5 is fixed and 1 is now measurable.
results.not_run: The LLM-sensitive assertions (c1, c2, c5 with and without the skill) require fresh contexts and a second model run; they are the protocol above, not a result. The deterministic assertions were run for real on the worked deck.

evals.prompt: I need a 15-minute conference talk deck for our paper. The paper is in ./paper.md and the plots are in ./figures/. The talk is in English.
assertions: A deck directory exists with a deck.py module that imports deckkit, and Deck(minutes=15) is set.

The empirical-CS genre profile was read: the spine runs task/application → prior limitations → insight → contribution → method → experiments → related work → conclusion, rather than the DSR defence spine.
The related-work slide cites the nearest neighbour explicitly, organised by topic rather than chronologically.
The contribution is stated as an unhedged claim on one slide, with the bound in the same breath — not the bound alone.
Result slides state n, the metric direction and the uncertainty, not a p-value alone (evidence-on-slides.md).
Every reproduced figure carries a visible source line and a `credit=`; every picture carries `alt=`.
The theme is derived from the palette used by the figures in ./figures, and the derivation is recorded in the theme's provenance field.
Every slide in the built .pptx has non-empty speaker notes containing a time budget and a quoted Sprechtext.
`deck build` exits 0 and `deck check` exits 0.
`deck timing` runs, reports the noted total against 15 minutes, and no slide's script is reported as long for its slot without a recorded decision.
A contact sheet exists under out/render/ and is newer than the .pptx.
Slide titles are assertions, not topics: at most two are a bare noun phrase.

evals.prompt: Build the deck for my design-science thesis defence. The chapters are in ./thesis/ and the examiners' written assessment is in ./gutachten.md.
assertions: The DSR/defence genre profile was read, not the empirical-CS or job-talk one.
The research question slide states a class of problems with the case named as the setting; applying the delete test leaves a question a field would still want answered.
A contribution slide claims in one unhedged sentence, names the contribution type (instantiation / construct / method / theory), and bounds it only after the claim.
The positioning slide names the construct each compared work operationalises, not only task/context/validation/outcomes.
The limitations are mapped to Wohlin's four validities, each with at least one named threat, and any confounded increment is named before it is asked about.
A backup slide maps each point of the written assessment to a stance and the evidence; its notes mark it as speaker-only.
`deck readiness` was run and the five questions in references/defence-readiness.md were answered with findings keyed to slide numbers.
`deck check` exits 0, and the closing slide ends on the answer to the research question rather than on a summary or on 'remains unresolved'.

evals.prompt: This deck is for our brand now, not the university. Brand primary is #B03A2E, secondary #2E5F8A. Re-theme it and show me what changed.
assertions: Only the theme JSON changed, or the change to deck.py is limited to the Theme.load() path; slide content is untouched.
The new theme defines every REQUIRED_ROLES entry and the emphasis_on_dark colour is legible against the new filled accent.
The deck is rebuilt and re-rendered, and a fresh contact sheet exists.
`deck check` still exits 0 after the re-theme.
The reply names at least one layout consequence rather than only reporting that the colours changed.

evals.prompt: can you make me a deck for my colloquium
assertions: The reply asks about language, duration, audience or what the deck must achieve before or while building, in one batched round rather than a sequence of single questions.
The reply identifies the genre (a defence/colloquium) or asks which of the genre profiles applies, rather than assuming one.
If the user does not answer, the reply proceeds and prints every assumption it made as a named default.
No deck is built with an invented duration or an inferred language that the request did not support.

evals.prompt: I have a faculty interview next month and need a 45-minute job talk from my research so far.
assertions: The job-talk genre profile was read, not the paper-talk or defence one: the spine runs problem → why it matters → what I have shown → the through-line → the next five years → how I work → why here.
The talk states a research identity in one sentence, and the past work is presented as a programme with an explicit through-line rather than a sequence of papers.
The agenda is concrete — directions with a first result, collaborator or dataset — not 'continue to explore'.
The closing slide returns to the research identity, not to a thank-you or a summary of the dissertation.
The talk does not spend the bulk of its time recapping the dissertation.
